site.lab_name: Synthetic Biology and BioProcess Engineering Lab
site.home_intro: The Synthetic Biology and Bioprocess Engineering Lab at Kyung Hee University (KHU) engineers microorganisms into cell factories for sustainable biomanufacturing. Our work runs along three connected lines. First, we build the foundational tools that make conventional and non-conventional hosts — bacteria, yeasts, microalgae, marine protists, and methanotrophs — as tractable as model organisms, developing synthetic biology tools. Second, we apply metabolic engineering to convert renewable carbon — CO2, methane, methanol, and lignocellulosic sugars — into various bioproducts: industrial chemicals and fuels (white biotechnology), pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals (red biotechnology), and food and feed materials (green biotechnology). Third, we are building an AI-driven, automated design–build–test–learn platform, so that strain development becomes a data-driven and increasingly self-directed process rather than a manual one. Together these efforts aim at bioprocesses that are not only environmentally sound but economically competitive.

topics.title: Development of foundational synthetic biology tools for diverse microorganisms
topics.body: Synthetic biology begins with the ability to modify an organism at will, and for most industrially attractive microorganisms, this ability is still limited. We build foundational toolkits that make conventional and non-conventional hosts as tractable as established model organisms. These include CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing and multiplex integration, modular cloning and in vivo DNA assembly, gene expression regulation, genetic circuits, and biosensors. We develop these tools across bacteria, yeasts, microalgae, marine protists, and methanotrophs. In each case, our aim is the same: to turn a promising but intractable organism into a well-characterized chassis upon which others can build.

topics.title: Metabolic engineering for white, red, and green bioproducts
topics.body: With the foundational tools in place, the question becomes what to make. Following the color conventions of industrial biotechnology, we redirect carbon flux in engineered strains toward three main product families. In White biotechnology, we focus on eco-friendly bioplastics, sustainable biofuels, and essential industrial chemicals. For Red biotechnology, our targets include high-value pharmaceuticals, health supplements, and functional biomolecules such as antioxidants and omega fatty acids. Finally, in Green biotechnology, we produce alternative proteins, sustainable animal feed, and natural food ingredients. To achieve this, we utilize renewable, strictly non-food feedstocks, including CO2, C1 carbon sources like methanol and formate, and agricultural biomass. While the same host organisms can serve all three fields, we tailor the genetic pathways, engineer key enzymes to overcome metabolic bottlenecks, and optimize the bioprocesses for each specific target. Ultimately, we treat enzyme engineering, genetic pathway design, cellular metabolism optimization, and industrial fermentation scaling as a single, unified engineering challenge, because a strain that succeeds only in a small-scale shake flask is not yet a truly useful result.

topics.title: AI-driven automation: biofoundry and the self-driving lab
topics.body: Strain engineering is still largely manual, and the design–build–test–learn (DBTL) cycle remains the rate-limiting step in biomanufacturing. We are building an automated, data-driven platform to shorten it: standardized genetic parts and assembly protocols that a liquid handler can execute, high-throughput cultivation and analytics that generate consistent phenotype data, and machine-learning models trained on that data to propose the next round of designs. Integrating these AI-assisted approaches with genome-scale metabolic models, our aim is to establish a biofoundry where the choice of the next experiment is driven by data rather than intuition—a significant step toward a self-driving laboratory for microbial cell factory development.
